title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 49
paragraphs: These cities, then, were preparing these things; and meanwhile, when the heralds had come to Hellas, many of those who lived on the mainland gave what the Persian demanded, and all those who lived on the islands did so, whomever the heralds came to with their demand. The islanders, I say, gave earth and water to Darius, and among them also those of Aegina. When these had done so, the Athenians at once went urgently against them, supposing that the Aeginetans had given in with hostile intent against themselves, so as to make an expedition against them together with the Persians; and they were also glad to get hold of a pretext against them. So they went back and forth to Sparta and accused the Aeginetans of what they had done, as having proved themselves traitors to Hellas.
